context: A mom walks her son home from school
purpose: Teach: 出口/ごみ/暗く/用事/食う/眺める/嫌わ/要ら

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、学校の出口で、ごみ拾いの当番だったんだよ。
lines.en: Mom, I was on litter duty at the school exit today.
lines.style: Eager, matter-of-fact report. Quick tempo, straightforward. Pride tucked under the surface — stating the fact itself lets adults know he did something good.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: えらいね。空が暗くなる前に終わってよかった。
lines.en: Good job. I'm glad you finished before it got dark.
lines.style: Warm approval, genuine. Soft warmth — not effusive, but solid. A small pause after 'good job,' letting it land. Practical concern underneath the praise.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 夕方、ママ用事あるって言ってたよね?
lines.en: You said you had an errand this evening, didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle check-in, not demanding. Quiet observation — he's already been thinking about her schedule. Small-voiced, attentive. Phrased as a question to confirm, not interrogate.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: うん、ちょっと買い物。何か食うもの、買おうか。
lines.en: Yeah, just a quick errand. Should we pick up something to eat while we're out?
lines.style: Casual, practical warmth. Light tempo. A mother thinking aloud with her son, not at him. Offers inclusion in the small decision.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: お父さんが嫌わないものがいいなあ。
lines.en: Something Dad won't hate would be nice.
lines.style: Soft, careful thought. Not worried, just quietly aware — he's considering everyone in the equation. Small voice, almost to himself. Perceptive in the way only observant kids are.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ふふ、雲を眺めるあなたの横顔、可愛いよ。
lines.en: Hehe, your little face looking up at those clouds is so sweet.
lines.style: Tender, half-amused. A quiet laugh. She's caught him in a moment of his own world. Softly affectionate — not performing emotion, just noticing him. Warmth that expects nothing back.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 傘、要らないよね、今日は。
lines.en: We won't need an umbrella today, will we?
lines.style: Light, observational. Almost thinking aloud. A small confirmation — checking the sky, checking the moment. Tone suggests he's already registered the weather and is just confirming with her.
